newsitem.title: CHINA: China corn sales seen slack through to end-1997.
newsitem.headline: China corn sales seen slack through to end-1997.

text.p: China's corn exports should remain slack for the rest of 1997, with sporadic sales to the Philippines and Vietnam likely to be the only activity, traders said on Monday.
The Philippines could pick up another 50,000 to 60,000 tonnes of Chinese grain for July/August delivery after taking 14,000 tonnes earlier this month, a trader in Singapore said.
Vietnam was likely to be looking for about 40,000 tonnes to bolster the local corn crop around December, traders said.
The 14,000-tonne deal to the Philippines was priced at $137-138 per tonne inclusive of cargo and freight (C&F), the trader who concluded the deal said.
This put the free on board (FOB) price at $122-123 per tonne at the northern Chinese port of Dalian, he said.
Other trading sources said the FOB Dalian corn price was still indicated at around $130 a tonne.
Most of the region was well covered for corn through to the end of the year, traders said.

Indonesia, where the corn crop was still coming in, could come back to the market in September, they said. No demand was seen in Malaysia, Thailand had exhausted its 200,000-tonne quota and Japan was not interested in the Chinese product, they said.
China has already sold more than two million tonnes of corn on the world market since the start of 1997, trade and industry sources have said.

The sales, the first since December 1994, began in January to ease over-stocked silos after a bumper crop in 1996 of up to 127 million tonnes, according to traders' estimates. No official figure has been released.
More than six million tonnes of the grain has been shipped from the northern growing regions to the southern consumption areas, official media have reported.

All indications are that China is heading for another record-breaking grain harvest in 1997. The official Xinhua news agency said on Sunday the summer grain harvest would be a record 118 million tonnes this year, up 3.5 percent on the 1996 figure.
Trade sources have said this fact alone should lead to higher exports of corn, which could hit three million tonnes for all of 1997 -- provided there are buyers.
